prompt: Which expression is the general antiderivative of $f(x) = 4x^3 + 2$?
hint: Antidifferentiation reverses the power rule: raise the exponent by one, then divide by the new exponent.

hints.text: Antidifferentiation reverses the power rule: raise the exponent by one, then divide by the new exponent.
$4x^3 \to \frac{4x^4}{4} = x^4$. The constant $2 \to 2x$. Do not forget $+ C$.
$x^4 + 2x + C$: choice A. Check by differentiating: $4x^3 + 2$. ✓

explanation: So the general antiderivative is $x^4 + 2x + C$, choice A.
Choice B is the DERIVATIVE of $f$, not an antiderivative; C forgot the $2$; D forgot to divide by the new exponent.

alternativeExplanations.title: Differentiate each choice
steps: The right answer must differentiate back to $4x^3 + 2$.
Only A passes. Differentiating to check is always available and takes seconds.
